text.p: Belgian speech recognition technology firm Lernout & Hauspie said in a statement on Tuesday it had completed its already announced acquisition of Kurzweil Applied Intelligence Inc of the U.S..
Under the deal, Kurzweil shareholders will receive approximately $40.7 million in cash and 460,000 shares of L&H stock.
Lernout & Hauspie said they expected the acquisition to have no impact on its 1997 earnings per share and to be accretive in 1998.

Lernout said the seventy five percent of the acquisition costs would be written off in the second quarter. The remaining 25 percent would be treated as goodwill and amortized over the next seven years.
It noted it would also book a $1.6 million charge in the second quarter to cover the costs of the merger.
Lernout said in the same statement it had cut the prices of Kurzweil's retail dictation products to keep its market share.
